tasks.title: Implement Bit and FixedWidthBits Ownership Model
tasks.description: Pre-allocate internal Bit array slots in FixedWidthBits to enforce exclusive ownership and prevent aliasing bugs when setting/getting bits.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. FixedWidthBits pre-allocates internal Bit array in constructor.
2. set(Bit[]) and set(int, Bit) perform deep copy of bit values.
3. set(String) updates existing owned slots.
4. Copy constructor performs full deep copy.

tasks.title: Implement Byte, Word, and Address Data Primitives
tasks.description: Implement Byte (8-bit), Word (32-bit), and Address (16-bit) types extending FixedWidthBits.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Byte constrained to 8 bits.
2. Word constrained to 32 bits.
3. Address constrained to 16 bits.
4. Conversion utilities to long/int and String operate accurately.
tasks.notes: Completed basic implementations in core package.

tasks.title: Implement LogicGates with Zero-Allocation API
tasks.description: Implement NOT, AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR logic gates with both allocating and destination-based (zero-allocation) overloads.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. LogicGates provides void destination-based methods for all gate types.
2. No allocations occur during destination-based gate executions.
3. Allocating methods preserved for unit tests.

tasks.title: Implement Half Adder and Full Adder Circuits
tasks.description: Build single-bit Half Adder (Sum, Carry) and Full Adder (Sum, CarryOut) using destination-based logic gates.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. HalfAdder calculates Sum = A XOR B, Carry = A AND B without object allocation.
2. FullAdder calculates Sum and CarryOut for A, B, CarryIn.
3. Complete unit test suite verifying truth tables for all input combinations.

tasks.title: Implement 32-Bit Word Adder and Subtractor
tasks.description: Cascade 32 Full Adders to construct a zero-allocation 32-bit Word adder/subtractor with Carry and Overflow output.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. 32-bit addition computes sum in destination Word.
2. Subtraction implemented using two's complement inversion + CarryIn=1.
3. Correct generation of CarryOut and Two's Complement Overflow signals.
4. Comprehensive unit tests covering boundary values (0, MaxInt, MinInt, overflow).
tasks.notes: Requires scratch bit pre-allocation in adder instance.

tasks.title: Implement Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
tasks.description: Construct 32-bit ALU supporting ADD, SUB, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, Shift Left, Shift Right, and flag generation (Z, N, C, V).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. ALU accepts two input Words, control op, and writes to output Word.
2. Sets Z (Zero), N (Negative), C (Carry), V (Overflow) flags accurately.
3. Execution is entirely zero-allocation.

tasks.title: Implement Register File and Special Registers
tasks.description: Implement 16 general-purpose 32-bit registers (R0-R15) and special registers (PC, SP, IR, FLAGS).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. RegisterFile allows indexed read/write of R0-R15.
2. Dedicated accessors for PC (16-bit address), SP (16-bit address), IR (Word), and FLAGS.
3. Reset method clears register state.

tasks.title: Implement 64 KiB Memory System
tasks.description: Implement 64 KiB byte-addressable RAM with 16-bit Address lookup, Word read/write (little-endian), and bounds checking.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. ReadByte / WriteByte at 16-bit Address.
2. ReadWord / WriteWord handles little-endian 4-byte encoding.
3. Out-of-bounds access throws explicit exception.

tasks.title: Define Instruction Set Architecture & Decoder
tasks.description: Specify instruction format, opcodes (MOV, LOAD, STORE, ADD, SUB, AND, OR, JMP, JZ, PUSH, POP, HALT), and instruction decoder.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Complete Opcode enum and bit layout specification.
2. InstructionDecoder converts raw Word into decoded Instruction record.
3. Verification test suite for encoding and decoding all instructions.
tasks.notes: Bridge between CPU hardware and software.

tasks.title: Migrate to Native 64-Bit Architecture & Extended ISA
tasks.description: Full architectural migration to native 64-bit system: 64-bit data words and registers, 64-bit fixed instruction format (8 bytes, PC += 8), 3-operand ALU operations (Rd = Rs1 OP Rs2), direct 32-bit embedded immediates, 8-bit opcode space (256 opcodes), 64-bit address space, expanded RAM capacity, hardware MUL/DIV, subroutines (CALL/RET), and sub-word memory access (LOADB, LOADH, LOADW, LOAD).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Word and Address expanded to 64-bit FixedWidthBits with deep bit-ownership invariants.
2. WordAdderSubtractor, WordMultiplier, and WordDivider execute 64-bit arithmetic with zero allocations.
3. 64-bit Instruction format [Opcode 8b][Flags/Cond 4b][Rd 6b][Rs1 6b][Rs2 6b][Imm32 32b] decoded by InstructionDecoder.
4. CPU fetch-decode-execute advances PC by 8 and executes 3-operand operations and 64-bit register reads/writes.
5. Sub-word memory access (LOADB/STOREB, LOADH/STOREH, LOADW/STOREW, LOAD/STORE 64-bit) implemented with little-endian encoding.
6. Assembler lexer/parser/resolver/encoder updated for 3-operand syntax (e.g., 'add r3, r1, r2'), 32-bit direct immediates, and 64-bit binary emission.
7. Test suite passes completely across all 64-bit core arithmetic, CPU execution, and assembler suites.
tasks.notes: Fundamental hardware foundation upgrade. Supersedes 32-bit legacy constraints before disassembler and compiler pipeline.

blueprint.goal: Transform TheComputer into a native 64-bit architecture with 64-bit data registers, 64-bit fixed instructions, 3-operand instructions, 32-bit immediates, 256 opcode slots, 64-bit address space, and expanded memory capacity.
scope_in: Data & Registers: Expand Word and Address to 64 bits (long backing); 32 GPRs of 64 bits (R0-R31); 64-bit PC (step +8), SP, and FLAGS.
Arithmetic circuits: 64-stage WordAdderSubtractor, 64-bit WordMultiplier, and 64-bit WordDivider in core.arithmetic with zero allocation.
Instruction Encoding (64 bits): [Opcode 8b][Cond 4b][Rd 6b][Rs1 6b][Rs2 6b][Imm32/Offset 32b][Reserved 2b].
3-Operand Format: Math ops support Rd = Rs1 OP Rs2 (non-destructive) alongside immediate forms (ADDI, SUBI).
ISA Extensions: MUL, DIV, MOD, CMP, CMPI, CALL, RET, JMP, conditional branches (JZ, JNZ, JG, JL, JGE, JLE), PUSH, POP, HALT.
Memory Sizing & Slicing: Sized RAM capacity (e.g. 1 MiB+), 8-byte word transfers, sub-word instructions: LOADB/STOREB (8b), LOADH/STOREH (16b), LOADW/STOREW (32b), LOAD/STORE (64b).
Assembler pipeline: Parser grammar for 3-operand instructions and 32-bit immediates; 8-byte machine word encoding.
scope_out: Paging MMU (MEM-002) — builds on top of 64-bit memory layout.
blueprint.topology: core.word.Word (64b) + core.arithmetic (64b Adder, Multiplier, Divider) -> cpu.registers (64b) + cpu.alu (64b 3-operand) -> isa (64b InstructionDecoder, 8b Opcode) -> cpu.Cpu (Fetch 8 bytes, execute) -> memory.ram.Ram (64b bus) -> assembler (3-operand 64b encoder).
steps: 1. Update Architecture constants: WORD_BITS=64, ADDRESS_BITS=64, INSTRUCTION_BYTES=8, MEMORY_SIZE_BYTES expansion.
2. Expand Word and Address to 64 bits, update WordAdderSubtractor to 64 FullAdders, implement 64-bit WordMultiplier and WordDivider.
3. Upgrade RegisterFile and SpecialRegisters to 64-bit Words/Addresses.
4. Redesign 64-bit Instruction record, 8-bit OpCode enum, and InstructionDecoder for 3-operand format and 32-bit immediates.
5. Update Cpu execute engine: PC increment (+8), 3-operand ALU dispatch, CALL/RET, sub-word load/stores.
6. Update Memory (Ram/SystemBus) for 64-bit word read/write and sub-word masks.
7. Update Assembler (Lexer, Parser, Resolver, Encoder) for 3-operand grammar and 64-bit binary emission.
8. Update test suites and verify complete 64-bit end-to-end execution.
hazards: Bit ownership: Ensure pre-allocated 64-bit arrays in Word/Address perform deep copies without aliasing.
Zero allocation: Pre-allocate 64-bit scratch buffers in ALU, Multiplier, and Divider.
Alignment: Instructions must align to 8-byte boundaries (PC % 8 == 0).
Little-endian byte slicing: Correct byte ordering across 1/2/4/8 byte memory operations.

tasks.title: Implement CPU Fetch-Decode-Execute Cycle
tasks.description: Implement CPU main loop driving Fetch (from PC), Decode, Execute via ALU/Memory, and Writeback.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Single-step execution executes one instruction and advances PC.
2. Execute loop runs until HALT instruction or interrupt.
3. Test execution of hand-encoded machine code programs.

tasks.title: Implement Dynamic Stack Limits & Boundary Guard
tasks.description: Implement dynamic STACK_BASE and STACK_LIMIT derived from Architecture.MEMORY_SIZE_BYTES and enforce StackOverflowException on stack boundary breaches during PUSH.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Dynamic calculation of STACK_BASE and STACK_LIMIT using MEMORY_SIZE_BYTES.
2. PUSH operation checks SP against STACK_LIMIT and throws StackOverflowException if breached.
3. Unit tests verifying stack boundary traps.

tasks.title: Implement MMU Guard Pages & Segmentation Fault Traps
tasks.description: Implement Memory Management Unit (MMU) with Guard Pages, page permission tables (R/W/X), and SegmentationFaultException.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Page table mapping with Read/Write/Execute permissions.
2. Guard Page detection triggering SegmentationFaultException.
3. Complete unit test coverage for memory protection traps.

tasks.title: Implement Motherboard & System Interconnect Host
tasks.description: Build Motherboard host assembling CPU, SystemBus, RamBusDevice, and RomBusDevice, and refactor BusDevice/AddressDecoder for relative address offset translation and reset lifecycle.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. AddressDecoder & BusDevice translate system addresses to device-relative offsets (systemAddress - startAddress).
2. BusDevice defines default reset() method, and SystemBus.reset() resets signal lines and all attached devices.
3. Ram supports sized capacity constructor (Ram(capacityBytes)).
4. Motherboard instantiates SystemBus, CPU, and handles system lifecycle (powerOn, reset, stepSystem, runSystem).
5. Complete unit test coverage.

tasks.title: Implement Assembler (Source → Machine)
tasks.description: Assembler pipeline: Lexer → Parser → Symbol resolution → Encoding → Output machine code.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Assemble simple programs to machine code.
2. Error messages point to source line.
3. Support labels and constants.

tasks.title: Implement Disassembler (Machine → Assembly)
tasks.description: Convert machine code back to readable assembly for debugging.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Disassemble machine code produced by assembler.
2. Preserve labels when possible.
3. Round-trip: assemble → disassemble → assemble reproduces identical bytes for every ISA instruction.
tasks.notes: Next ticket. Gates DBG-001 (the debugger's readable-assembly view is disassembly) and backs the GUI's Live Disassembly panel, which currently decodes ad-hoc.

blueprint.goal: A disassembler that decodes 32-bit machine words back into canonical assembly (mnemonic + operands) — the inverse of the assembler's encoder — driven by the same ISA opcode/operand-format tables so encode and decode can never drift.
scope_in: Decode one machine word into a structured instruction (opcode, operands with roles, addressing mode).
Render a decoded instruction to canonical assembly text matching the assembler's own syntax.
Disassemble a buffer/range into address-annotated (address, word, text) listing rows.
Reuse ISA-001's opcode + operand-format definitions as the single source of truth for both directions.
Deterministic, non-throwing handling of unknown/illegal encodings (emit a data directive / .word, never crash).
scope_out: Full symbol/label reconstruction (best-effort only; real symbolization needs a symbol table / debug info — future).
GUI and debugger wiring (they consume this module).
Decoding privileged/interrupt instructions from ADV-001 (not yet defined).
blueprint.topology: isa (opcode & operand-format tables) -> assembly.disassembler -> consumed by debugger + gui. One-way deps; the disassembler reads ONLY ISA definitions and raw words, never live CPU/memory runtime state. It is the mirror image of the assembler encoder and should share its ISA table.
steps: Confirm/expose an ISA-001 opcode+operand-format table usable in both directions (encode and decode).
Define decode(word) -> DecodedInstruction (opcode, ordered operands with roles/widths).
Define render(DecodedInstruction) -> assembly string in the assembler's canonical syntax.
Add range disassembly producing (address, word, text) rows for listings/the GUI panel.
Handle illegal/unknown opcodes deterministically as a data directive; no exceptions on arbitrary bytes.
Round-trip tests over every ISA instruction: text -> encode -> bytes -> disassemble -> encode again == identical bytes.
hazards: Encode/decode drift: the killer risk — the disassembler MUST share ISA-001's opcode table, not hardcode its own.
Immediate sign-extension and operand bit-widths must match the encoder exactly.
Endianness / word order must match the assembler and memory layout.
Unknown opcodes must degrade gracefully — the debugger will feed it arbitrary memory bytes, not just valid programs.

tasks.title: Implement Debugger (step, breakpoints, views)
tasks.description: Provide step execution, breakpoints, register/memory/stack views, and basic watch expressions.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Step through instructions and inspect registers & memory.
2. Set/clear breakpoints.
3. Present human-readable assembly alongside machine code.
tasks.notes: Essential for development productivity. Formalizes the ad-hoc step/run/watch logic currently living in the vibecoded GUI workbench into a real module the GUI can consume.

blueprint.goal: A headless debugger core that drives the existing CPU/Motherboard through controlled execution (single-step, run-to-halt, run-to-breakpoint) and exposes read-only inspection of registers, flags, memory, and the stack — with no debug logic living in the GUI.
scope_in: Debugger controller wrapping Motherboard/Cpu lifecycle (attach, step, run, pause, reset).
Breakpoint set keyed by instruction address; execution halts before executing a break address.
Read-only inspection snapshots: register file, PC/SP/IR, ALU flags (Z/N/C/V), memory window, stack window.
Watch expressions over registers and absolute addresses (the GUI Watch panel already models this).
Human-readable disassembly of the current instruction (delegate to DIS-001 when available; interim: local decode).
scope_out: GUI wiring (separate; GUI consumes this module).
Source-level / symbolic debugging (needs debug info from the compiler chain).
Reverse execution, conditional breakpoints, data watchpoints (future).
blueprint.topology: gui -> debugger -> cpu -> memory -> isa. Debugger sits above the CPU cycle, observing via existing read APIs; it must never mutate architectural state except through the CPU's own step entrypoint. Layer isolation preserved (one-way deps).
steps: Define a Debugger controller interface: attach(Motherboard), step(), run(maxSteps), addBreakpoint(addr), removeBreakpoint(addr), state().
Introduce an immutable inspection snapshot type (registers, special regs, flags, decoded current instruction) built from existing getters — no new aliasing of Bit objects.
Implement the run loop as repeated single-steps guarded by a breakpoint check on PC before each fetch; stop on HALT, breakpoint hit, or step budget.
Add watch-expression evaluation: parse the same targets the GUI accepts (rN, sp, pc, 0xADDR) and resolve against the snapshot.
Wire disassembly of the current instruction; keep a seam so DIS-001 can replace the interim decoder.
Cover with unit tests: breakpoint halts before the target executes, step advances exactly one instruction, snapshots reflect post-step state.
hazards: Bit ownership: snapshots must deep-copy values, never share Bit objects with the live register file/memory.
Zero-allocation contract in the hot path stays in core/cpu — the debugger observes, it does not run inside the ALU/adder inner loops.
Breakpoint semantics: halt BEFORE executing the break address (pre-fetch), not after, or stepping past a breakpoint becomes ambiguous.
Run budget to avoid infinite loops on programs without HALT.

tasks.title: Implement CPU Cache Hierarchy (L1 -> L2 -> L3)
tasks.description: Cache layer between CPU and main memory to cut access latency. Start with one simple L1; architected so L2/L3 chain in without touching CPU or RAM.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. L1 read hit/miss + fill works; results identical to running without cache.
2. Hit/miss statistics exposed.
3. Transparent: a program's final state is byte-identical with and without the cache.
4. Later phases add L2, L3, set-associativity, write-back, LRU.
tasks.notes: Start simple (single direct-mapped write-through L1), grow to full L1/L2/L3.

blueprint.goal: A cache hierarchy on the CPU<->memory path that reduces effective memory latency, beginning with a single simple L1 and structured so L2 and L3 slot in as a chain with no changes to the CPU or RAM.
scope_in: Phase 1: single L1, direct-mapped, write-through + no-write-allocate.
Tag/index/offset decode from a 16-bit Address; line fill on read miss.
Same read/write(Address, Word) interface as a bus device so it is transparent to the CPU.
Hit/miss counters and a simple stats view.
Optional wiring into Motherboard between CPU and SystemBus.
Later phases: L2 then L3 by chaining; set-associativity + LRU; write-back/write-allocate.
scope_out: Cross-core cache coherence (owned by the multicore ticket, later phase).
blueprint.topology: cpu -> cache(L1[-L2[-L3]]) -> systembus -> ram. Each cache level implements the same read/write(Address, Word) contract as the bus and holds a reference to the next level; chaining levels needs no CPU change. Cache is transparent: identical observable results with or without it.
steps: Define a CacheLevel abstraction: read(Address, Word dst), write(Address, Word), backed by the next level (cache or bus).
Implement direct-mapped L1: partition Address into tag/index/offset; on read miss, fill the line from the next level; on write, write-through to next level.
Preallocate line storage (owned Word slots) so steady-state is zero-allocation.
Expose hit/miss stats.
Optionally insert L1 between CPU and SystemBus in Motherboard behind a flag.
Verify transparency: run programs with and without cache, assert byte-identical final memory + registers.
Later: parametrize associativity + replacement (LRU) + write-back; add L2/L3 by chaining.
hazards: Bit ownership: cache lines must deep-copy Word/Bit values, never alias RAM's or the CPU's Bit objects.
16-bit Address partition (tag/index/offset) must be exact and total.
Write-through vs write-back correctness and ordering to the next level.
Steady-state zero allocation: preallocate lines, no per-access heap objects.
Transparency is the invariant: cache must never change program-visible results.

tasks.title: Implement Multicore CPU (SMP, N cores, shared bus)
tasks.description: Multiple CPU cores sharing one SystemBus + RAM (SMP), configurable core count (>2). Deterministic stepping first; parallel + cache coherence later. Includes step-path optimization.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Motherboard hosts N cores (N configurable, >2) sharing one bus + RAM.
2. Each core has independent register file / PC / SP; no shared mutable Bit/register state.
3. System step advances each non-halted core one instruction deterministically; run stops when all cores halt.
4. Per-core state inspectable (for GUI).
5. Step path allocation-free (perf).
tasks.notes: Start deterministic sequential stepping across cores; cache coherence (MESI) is a later phase gated on CACHE-001. Step optimization required: the CPU step path must be zero-allocation so N cores x many steps stays fast.

blueprint.goal: Turn the single-core machine into an SMP multicore: N CPU cores (configurable, more than 2) sharing one SystemBus and RAM, stepped deterministically, as the foundation for later cache coherence and parallel execution.
scope_in: Generalize Motherboard from one Cpu to a Cpu[] (configurable N).
Each core owns its own SpecialRegisters + RegisterFile; only the bus + RAM are shared.
stepSystem() advances each non-halted core one instruction per tick (round-robin / lockstep).
runSystem() runs until all cores halt; per-core HALT tracked.
Expose per-core state for the GUI.
Step-path optimization: eliminate per-step heap allocation so N cores scale.
scope_out: Cache coherence / MESI (later phase, depends on CACHE-001).
True OS-thread parallelism (start with deterministic sequential stepping).
blueprint.topology: motherboard -> Cpu[0..N-1] -> shared SystemBus -> RAM. Cores hold independent register/PC/SP state; memory is shared. Later: per-core L1 cache (CACHE-001) + a coherence protocol (MESI) arbitrated over the shared bus.
steps: Refactor Motherboard to hold and manage a Cpu[] with lifecycle (powerOn/reset/step/run) over all cores.
Confirm each Cpu instance owns exclusive register/special-register state (no shared mutable Bit objects across cores).
Implement deterministic stepSystem(): iterate cores in fixed order, step each non-halted core once.
Implement runSystem(): loop stepSystem() until every core is halted (with a step budget).
Optimize the single-core step path to zero-allocation (reuse preallocated Word/Address scratch) so N cores stay fast.
Expose per-core snapshots for the GUI.
Later phase: add per-core L1 + MESI coherence over the shared bus.
hazards: No shared Bit/register objects across cores - each core's state must be exclusively owned (ownership invariant).
Deterministic step order required while stepping is sequential; document it before any real parallelism.
Shared-memory races appear once execution is truly parallel - keep sequential first, add synchronization deliberately.
Performance amplification: N cores x steps multiplies any per-step allocation - the step path MUST be zero-allocation.
GUI must scale to N cores without per-step full rebuilds (ties to the GUI memory-view perf fix).
